newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac says yr started well, outlook good.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac says yr started well, outlook good.

text.p: British construction group Tarmac Plc said on Tuesday it had made a good start to the year with recovery underway in most of its domestic markets.
Tarmac said the industry was looking at substantial contracts from public and private partnerships and noted that lottery-funded and millennium projects were advancing.
"With major rail infrastructure work planned, the opportunities in construction over the next few years are looking brighter," chairman John Banham told the annual shareholder meeting.
Banham said he was encouraged by the actions of the new Labour government.

"We believe that there will be additional opportunities from the restructuring of the Private Finance Initiative and from the release of local authority housing receipts for social housing, although the full effects may not be immediate," Banham said.

Banham said the British quarrying business saw average volumes rise modestly in the first five months of the current year, helped by better weather in the first quarter. Prices improved and there was scope for more price rises, he said.
Banham said volumes and prices were up in Tarmac's ready-mix concrete and concrete block operations, helped by the better British housing market.
In North America, volumes and prices were ahead but there was some regional weakness.
Banham said strong orders at Tarmac Construction enabled it to push for better margins on tenders but competition remained tough.
